title: Default Effects of Credit Card Minimum Payments
eligible_reason: Matched-control DiD in event time (six months pre and post a card's switch to automatic minimum payment, control = Mahalanobis-matched nonswitching card-months). Estimated as a single-hurdle Type II Tobit selection model with exp() second stage, time-varying covariates, and Switcher x months-from-switch dummies. No unit or calendar-time fixed effects. Also IV and a lab experiment.
design_notes: JMR 59(4), 2022. Section 'Difference-in-Differences Estimates' (Figure 2, Table 6): outcome = monthly repayment amount per card; treatment = Switcher_i x D_{i,t} (dummies for months -5..+5 from switch); covariates include card balance, utilization, spending, merchant APR, cash APR, charge-off rate (time-varying) and tenure. Matching per Ho et al. 2011; 3,311 treated and 3,239 control cards, 39,732 card-months per group. Table 7 is IV (peer switching rate); Table 8 onward is a randomized experiment. Calendar switch dates vary (Jan 2013 to Nov 2014) but the estimator is event-time with matched controls, nonlinear, with controls.
screener_notes: Not eligible. Matching-based DiD, nonlinear selection model, time-varying controls, no unit and calendar FE. Data from U.K. card issuers via Argus Information & Advisory; paper states data are proprietary. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only.
